title: A high schooler
building at the
edge of curiosity.
paragraphs: I started writing HTML in 2020. The world had gone quiet: lockdowns, closed schools, an entire childhood paused, and I opened a YouTube tab and taught myself what <html> did. I haven't stopped since.

By grade nine I was building crowd-sourced civic tools. By grade eleven I was reporting security flaws to a national news broadcaster. Now I'm in grade twelve, learning the MERN stack, and breaking applications to understand how they think.
I compete in hackathons. I win some. I learn from all of them. I care about three things: shipped products, clean code, and the human on the other end of the screen.

title: Selected
projects.
work.intro: Five projects. Each one was built for a real problem, demoed in front of judges, and pushed past the prototype stage. They live in hackathon halls and school exhibitions — not in tutorial folders.

projects.title: Sastomahango
projects.description: A crowd-sourced price index for everyday goods. Users report what they paid, the system aggregates prices by locality, and shoppers see whether they're about to get scammed at the bazaar. Built to fight the opacity of Kathmandu's informal markets.

projects.title: Lifeline
projects.description: An off-grid, RF-based emergency signal system. When there's no cellular coverage — landslides, remote valleys, the post-quake window — Lifeline transmits short distress beacons across radio so a receiver in a populated area can relay them to first responders.

projects.title: Sawari
projects.description: A complete public transport companion for Kathmandu. Enter where you are, enter where you want to go, and Sawari hands you the full walkthrough — the bus, the route, the fare, the road condition, the ETA. Built around the city's actual, chaotic network.

projects.title: AgroPan
projects.description: A soil monitoring and crop recommendation rig. Sensor arrays measure moisture, pH, and nutrients in the field; AgroPan returns a crop recommendation tailored to what's actually in the ground — not what the seed shop is selling.

projects.title: Edu Track Pro
projects.description: A smart attendance system for Nepali schools. Every student taps their ID card on an RFID reader at the gate, attendance is logged instantly, and class teachers see who's actually in the room. Built to replace the paper register that's still standard here.

title: Tools I
work with.
stack.intro: I started with the boring fundamentals and I still respect them. The list grows on purpose — only when something earns its place in a real project.

title: Security
research.
research.intro: Bug hunting is a way of reading. Every application is a story about assumptions, and some of those assumptions are wrong. Below are the ones I found and disclosed.

disclosures.title: Critical flaw on Kantipur.tv
disclosures.description: A critical issue on the website of one of Nepal's largest news broadcasters. Reported through the proper disclosure channel, acknowledged, and patched upstream.

disclosures.title: Bug in Monkeytype
disclosures.description: A flaw in the popular open-source typing utility used by tens of thousands of typists worldwide. Reported, acknowledged, and patched upstream.

title: Let's build
something.
contact.intro: Open to collaborations, hackathon teams, internships, and interesting security disclosures. If you're working on something that actually matters to people, I'd like to hear about it.

projects.title: Sastomahango
projects.description: A crowd-sourced price index for everyday goods. Users report what they paid, the system aggregates prices by locality, and shoppers see whether they're about to get scammed at the bazaar. Built to fight the opacity of Kathmandu's informal markets.
projects.longDescription: Sastomahango was built to address the lack of transparent pricing in traditional Nepali retail and vegetable markets (Bazaars). By allowing shoppers across various municipal wards to submit crowdsourced prices and receipts in real time, the platform calculates median price corridors and alerts consumers about sudden artificial inflation.

projects.title: Lifeline
projects.description: An off-grid, RF-based emergency signal system. When there's no cellular coverage — landslides, remote valleys, the post-quake window — Lifeline transmits short distress beacons across radio so a receiver in a populated area can relay them to first responders.
projects.longDescription: Designed specifically for Nepal's challenging Himalayan topography and disaster vulnerability. Lifeline operates on unlicensed sub-GHz ISM radio bands, broadcasting ultra-low-power distress packets containing GPS coordinates and casualty status without relying on cellular towers or internet infrastructure.

projects.title: Sawari
projects.description: A complete public transport companion for Kathmandu. Enter where you are, enter where you want to go, and Sawari hands you the full walkthrough — the bus, the route, the fare, the road condition, the ETA. Built around the city's actual, chaotic network.
projects.longDescription: Kathmandu's public transit network lacks official schedules and centralized route maps. Sawari models microbus routes, Sajha Yatayat lines, and tempo corridors with localized graph algorithms to provide multi-modal route guidance, accurate fare estimates, and transfer hints.

projects.title: AgroPan
projects.description: A soil monitoring and crop recommendation rig. Sensor arrays measure moisture, pH, and nutrients in the field; AgroPan returns a crop recommendation tailored to what's actually in the ground — not what the seed shop is selling.
projects.longDescription: AgroPan combines multi-parameter NPK soil sensor probes with ESP microcontroller nodes to measure real-time soil chemistry. Data is transmitted to a local dashboard that matches environmental parameters against regional agronomic datasets for optimal seasonal crop selection.

projects.title: Edu Track Pro
projects.description: A smart attendance system for Nepali schools. Every student taps their ID card on an RFID reader at the gate, attendance is logged instantly, and class teachers see who's actually in the room. Built to replace the paper register that's still standard here.
projects.longDescription: Paper roll-calls consume significant classroom teaching time in government and private secondary schools. EduTrack Pro deploys high-frequency RFID scanners with local edge caching to log 1,000+ student arrivals per hour, automatically generating SMS notices to parents and daily analytics for headmasters.

projects.title: Kantipur TV Vulnerability Disclosure
projects.description: Responsible vulnerability disclosure of a critical authentication boundary bypass on the web platform of Kantipur Television, one of Nepal's foremost national news organisations.
projects.longDescription: Identified an access control flaw allowing unauthorized administrative access. Coordinated responsibly with the technical infrastructure team at Kantipur Television to verify the root cause and validate the patch before publication.

projects.title: Monkeytype Logic Patch
projects.description: Identified and reported a client-side execution anomaly in the globally popular open-source typing speed platform used by tens of thousands of typists.
projects.longDescription: Discovered an edge-case logic flaw during typing session telemetry processing. Submitted detailed steps to reproduce to the open-source repository maintainers, which was confirmed and merged into the main release.

projects.title: MeshPacket Radio Node
projects.description: A portable packet radio communicator for localized peer-to-peer text exchange during power blackouts and network outages.
projects.longDescription: Built with custom 3D-printed enclosure, 18650 lithium power management, OLED display, and keyboard module. Communicates over 433MHz / 915MHz LoRa mesh with end-to-end symmetric encryption.

projects.title: Civic Portal Header Audit
projects.description: An automated reconnaissance script evaluating HTTP security headers, SSL cipher configurations, and exposed endpoints on public municipal websites.
projects.longDescription: A command-line tool written in Python & Bash that audits security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, CORS) across government web assets to identify misconfigurations and produce remediation checklists.
